sourcedFrom: BANISH 30 GOLD — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED (NOT PRINTED)
cleanIntro: An 8.2 inch, 13.2 oz titanium .30 can that does NOT thread to the barrel: it quick-detaches onto a 5/8x24 muzzle brake that has to be timed onto the host with a shim kit first. Inside are 10 indexed baffles plus one accuracy baffle — the one with four holes and no centre cut — and an expansion spacer. Full-auto rated and rated from rimfire up to .300RUM, with the end cap coated in Tribodone 41 DLC to stop titanium-on-titanium galling.

steps.title: Clear the host, using the host's own manual
steps.action: Unload the rifle and open the action so the chamber is visibly clear before anything is unscrewed. Banish deliberately does not print a clearing sequence — it refers you to your own firearm's manual, which is the only document that knows your action.
steps.prose: Do it before the brake and the can are in your hands. Timing a brake is fiddly work and it should not be happening over a loaded rifle.
steps.quote: If you are at all unsure as to the proper procedures to ensure that your firearm is unloaded, please consult your firearm user’s manual/instructions and/or contact a properly licensed dealer or the manufacturer of your firearm.
steps.cite: BANISH 30 GOLD — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: The host firearm's manual is the clearing authority.

steps.title: Banish 30 Gold range — rimfire up to .300RUM
steps.action: Check the host cartridge against the rating. Banish rates the 30-GOLD for rimfire through .300RUM and calls it full-auto rated in the SPECS block, which is a wider and higher rating than the plain Banish 30's .300 Weatherby ceiling. It is the same bore class and NOT the same limit — do not carry either figure across to the other can.
steps.prose: The .300RUM figure is what the brake-mounted design buys: the quick-detach interface takes the load off the barrel threads.
steps.quote: It is rated for rimfire to .300RUM.
steps.cite: BANISH 30 GOLD — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — SPECS, p.3
steps.warn: Rimfire to .300RUM for THIS can. The plain Banish 30 stops at .300 WBY MAG.

steps.title: ⛔ This is a quick-detach can — the muzzle brake is the mount
steps.action: Understand the architecture before you touch it. The 30-GOLD ships with a 5/8x24 muzzle brake and a shim kit for timing that brake, and the can attaches to the brake rather than to the barrel. Everything about installation, alignment and removal on this can runs through that brake.
steps.prose: Banish's own SPECS line reads MOUNT STYLE: QD MUZZLE BRAKE. If you are looking for barrel threads on the back of this can, you are looking at the wrong product.
steps.quote: The Banish 30-GOLD comes as an 8.2-inch quick-detach suppressor holding eleven STifle™ baffles. It comes with a 5/8×24 muzzle break and shim kit for timing your brake.
steps.cite: BANISH 30 GOLD — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — SPECS, p.3

steps.title: Check the mount is fully shouldered before firing
steps.action: Look at the joint where the suppressor's thread mount meets the shoulder it seats against. Banish requires it fully shouldered with NO visible gap, and any crush washer left behind by a previous muzzle device has to be gone. On this can the mount lands on the supplied 5/8x24 muzzle brake, so the brake itself must have been shouldered and timed onto the barrel with its shim kit first.
steps.prose: Note what this book does NOT say: unlike the plain Banish 30 manual, the 30-GOLD's warning page carries no separate quick-detach paragraph. Its fit rule is the one sentence below and it applies to the joint you can see.
steps.quote: Check the fit between your barrel and silencer before firing! The thread mount must be fully shouldered on the barrel. There should be no visible gap between the barrel shoulder and the face of the silencer thread mount (crush washer from muzzle brake must be removed).
steps.cite: BANISH 30 GOLD — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: If there is any gap DO NOT fire the host with the silencer attached.

steps.title: Let it cool before you handle it
steps.action: After firing, the can is hot enough to burn. Banish tells you to use extreme caution removing it and offers a Devour cover or gloves. On a full-auto rated can this is not theoretical — sustained fire puts a lot of energy into 13.2 oz of titanium.
steps.prose: The brake underneath it is hotter still, and it is the part your hand goes past to reach the can.
steps.quote: When removing the silencer, use extreme caution as it may be hot to the touch after firing.
steps.cite: BANISH 30 GOLD — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: Gloves or a cover. Titanium gives no visual warning.

steps.title: Take the 30-GOLD off the brake, leave the brake on the barrel
steps.action: Unscrew the can from the muzzle brake and stop there. The brake stays where it is: it was shouldered by hand, timed to 12 o'clock with shims, then removed, dosed with Red Loctite or Rocksett and reset. Breaking that joint means redoing the whole timing sequence.
steps.prose: Banish's own instruction is to unscrew the can to remove it from the host — the brake is not part of that operation.
steps.caution: The brake is bonded on with Red Loctite or Rocksett. It does not come off casually.
steps.quote: To disassemble, make sure the firearm is unloaded and unscrew to remove from host firearm.
steps.cite: BANISH 30 GOLD — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — DISASSEMBLY AND CLEANING, p.5

steps.title: Clean the barrel threads before anything goes back on
steps.action: If the brake ever does come off, the first thing Banish asks for is clean threads. Fouling under a timed brake is exactly what makes a shim stack read wrong, and the timing is what sets the can's alignment to the bore.
steps.prose: That is step one of the brake procedure and it is the only step in it that also applies routinely.
steps.quote: 1. Make sure to clean the threads of your barrel prior to installation of muzzle brake.
steps.cite: BANISH 30 GOLD — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — INSTALLATION OF MUZZLE BRAKE AND SUPPRESSOR, p.4

steps.title: Never fire an obstructed can
steps.action: Look through the can before it goes back onto the brake. Mud, dirt, a patch or solvent still standing inside are all obstructions and Banish forbids firing through any of them. After a 24 hour soak this is the check that catches trapped solvent.
steps.prose: An 8.2 inch tube holds more liquid than it looks like it does, and none of it is visible from the outside.
steps.quote: Silencers must be free of obstructions such as mud, dirt, etc. DO NOT attempt to shoot through an obstructed silencer.
steps.cite: BANISH 30 GOLD — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: Sight through it every time before it goes on.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The 30-GOLD is off the brake and the brake is still timed on the barrel — that is the routine strip. The eleven-baffle teardown is the Deep Clean, and Banish sets the interval at every 50 to 100 rounds. It also warns off one ammunition class: solid lead or plated lead bullets are not recommended in this can.
steps.prose: Fifty to a hundred rounds is a short interval for a centrefire can, and it is short because the deep clean is the only way to reach the stack.
steps.aside: Quoted as the extraction renders it — the printed range is 50 - 100 and the hyphen drops out.
steps.quote: It is recommended that the suppressor be cleaned every 50 100 rounds fired. The use of solid lead or plated lead bullets is not recommended.
steps.cite: BANISH 30 GOLD — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — DISASSEMBLY AND CLEANING, p.5

deepSteps.title: End cap off — tool key and a T-45 torx
deepSteps.action: With the can off the host and the host unloaded, fit the supplied tool key together with a T-45 torx wrench and unscrew the end cap. Banish suggests JB Welding the torx and the key together permanently, which tells you how easily the two-piece tool slips on its own.
deepSteps.prose: That end cap is coated in Tribodone 41 DLC specifically to stop titanium galling on titanium. Damaging its tool interface is how you lose access to the can.
deepSteps.quote: Using the provided tool key and T-45 torx wrench, remove the end cap of the suppressor. For best results, we recommend permanently attaching the T-45 torx wrench and the tool key together. This can be done with “JB Weld” or similar product found at any local hardware store.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 30 GOLD — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — DISASSEMBLY AND CLEANING, p.5

deepSteps.title: Soak 24 hours, then push the stack out
deepSteps.action: Spray solvent through the inside and leave it a full 24 hours before anything moves. Then push the baffles out with a wooden dowel or Banish's optional Baffle Removal Tool. Driving a dry, carbon-locked stack scores both the baffles and the tube wall they index against.
deepSteps.prose: Wood, not steel. The tube's inner surface is the reference every baffle sits against.
deepSteps.caution: Twenty-four hours of soak before any force.
deepSteps.quote: Using your solvent of choice, spray the inside of the suppressor and let sit for 24 hours.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 30 GOLD — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — DISASSEMBLY AND CLEANING, p.5

deepSteps.title: Ten indexed baffles and ONE accuracy baffle — know which is which
deepSteps.action: As the stack comes out, identify the odd one. This can holds 10 indexed baffles plus a single accuracy baffle, and Banish identifies the accuracy baffle by its four holes and its lack of a centre cut. The indexed ten all have a centre cut and must fit together; the accuracy baffle does not and sits on top of them.
deepSteps.prose: Get that one part in the wrong place and the stack cannot index. Set it aside as it comes out rather than trusting yourself to spot it later.
deepSteps.quote: The suppressor has 10 indexed baffles and one accuracy baffle (indicated by the four holes and no center cut). Care must be taken when reassembling.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 30 GOLD — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — DISASSEMBLY AND CLEANING, p.5
deepSteps.warn: Four holes, no centre cut — that is the accuracy baffle, and there is only one.

deepSteps.title: Brass or nylon brush, then get all the solvent out
deepSteps.action: Scrub the baffles and the inside of the tube with a stiff brass or nylon brush and solvent or carbon killer. Then check every part is clean and that no solvent remains anywhere in the can before it is put back together.
deepSteps.prose: On a can with an o-ring in the end cap, trapped solvent has somewhere to hide. Drain it muzzle down and give it time.
deepSteps.quote: Use a stiff bristle brush (brass or nylon) with solvent / carbon killer of choice to clean the baffles and inside the tube.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 30 GOLD — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — DISASSEMBLY AND CLEANING, p.5
deepSteps.warn: Make sure all parts are clean and solvent has been removed.

deepSteps.title: Restack — ten indexed, then the accuracy baffle, then the spacer
deepSteps.action: On a flat surface stack the 10 indexed baffles on each other, place the accuracy baffle on top of them, and put the expansion spacer LAST on the stack. Every indexing tab has to be aligned and fully engaged with the baffle below it. Then slide the tube down over the stack, take it to the edge of the table and push the baffles up with one finger.
deepSteps.prose: That order is not interchangeable. The accuracy baffle's four holes work at the front of the stack and nowhere else.
deepSteps.quote: Using a flat surface, stack the 10 indexed baffles on top of each other, then place the accuracy baffle on top, and the expansion spacer last on the baffle stack. Make sure the indexing tabs are aligned and fully engaged in each corresponding baffles.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 30 GOLD — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — ASSEMBLY, p.6

deepSteps.title: Anti-seize, the 1/32 inch tell, then 110-120 inch pounds
deepSteps.action: Flip the assembly open end up and apply anti-seize to the threads before the end cap goes on. Tighten lightly first: with the baffles indexed, only the EDGE of the end cap shows, about 1/32 of an inch. More than that means the tabs are not aligned — take it apart rather than torquing it. Then finish at 110 to 120 inch pounds.
deepSteps.prose: The expansion spacer does not have to come out for cleaning at all, which is worth knowing: leaving it in place removes one thing that can be mis-stacked.
deepSteps.quote: Lightly tighten the end cap, when the baffles are properly aligned only the edge of the end cap will be exposed (approximately 1/32”).
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 30 GOLD — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — ASSEMBLY, p.6
deepSteps.warn: Finish tightening end cap to 110 - 120 inch pounds — and never torque a misaligned stack.

cleaning.name: BAFFLE STACK
tasks: Soak the interior with solvent for 24 hours before pushing anything out
Push the stack out with a wooden dowel or the Baffle Removal Tool
Identify the accuracy baffle by its four holes and absence of a centre cut and keep it separate
Scrub all eleven baffles and the tube interior with a stiff brass or nylon brush
Confirm no solvent is left anywhere before rebuilding

cleaning.name: END CAP
tasks: Use the tool key with a T-45 torx wrench
Apply anti-seize to the threads before refitting
Check only the edge of the cap shows, about 1/32 inch, before applying torque
The cap is Tribodone 41 DLC coated to prevent titanium galling — do not abrade it

cleaning.name: MUZZLE BRAKE MOUNT
tasks: Clean the barrel threads before any brake installation
Confirm the brake is still seated to the shoulder and correctly timed with its shims
Leave the brake bonded in place; retiming is a full procedure, not an adjustment
Check the attachment after 30 discharges — this book's interval, not the 5-then-30 the plain Banish 30 uses

cleaning.name: SCHEDULE AND AMMUNITION
tasks: Do not use solid lead or plated lead bullets in this can

reassembly: Stack the 10 indexed baffles with every indexing tab aligned and fully engaged.
Place the accuracy baffle — four holes, no centre cut — on top of the ten, then the expansion spacer last.
Slide the tube over the stack, take it to the edge of the table and push the baffles up the tube with one finger.
Flip the assembly open end up and apply anti-seize to the threads before installing the end cap.
Tighten lightly and confirm only the edge of the cap shows at about 1/32 inch; if more shows, the tabs are not aligned.
Finish tightening the end cap to 110 to 120 inch pounds, then fit the can back onto the timed muzzle brake.
fncheck: After rebuilding, confirm only the edge of the end cap is exposed, roughly 1/32 inch — anything more means the eleven-baffle stack is not indexed and the can must not be fired. Sight through the bore for one clear channel with no step and no standing solvent. On the rifle, confirm the muzzle brake is still seated to the shoulder and timed, and that the can has drawn up tight on it with no gap, and re-check that attachment after 30 discharges, which is the interval THIS manual prints.
